My response to someone posting the SR-71 Blackbird story:

Love this story.

I haven't had "that" moment being a member of a team or a crew, but I've had similar moments where we were on the same wavelength.

I think I've already told this story, nope, I didn't. It happened during that battle.

We take up positions cordoning off this huge area, the Minaret - 3rd image result in Jewgle, and our vehice and the vehicle next to us got hit by an IED. The commander of the vehicle beside us was looking over the edge of the vehicle and got his carotid artery cut open in the blast. Oh shit, he was certainly dead. Medic was in the PSG vehicle, and they rushed over, after hesitation, and grabbed him up, fled to the rear. Creepiest netcall I'd ever heard, because his throat was gushing blood while he was trying to talk on the net.

The site was a mosque, so we had to wait for the Iraqi Army to move in to take the site. Holy sites and all being off limits. While sitting there out in the open, we started taking mortar fire. I could see it through my periscope. about 200 meters away.... 150m away... My vehicle commander calls it up. 100m away, in a straight line towards our two vehicles. "They're fucking walking them in on us, we need to move!" I shout, just as higher up responds, "Hold your position, do not move."

I lit up a cigarette. 50m away, looks like it's right outside the fucking vehicle... And then it stops. It was rhythmic, every few seconds they'd drop one closer and closer... but the rhythm stopped right there, outside of our vehicle. No explanation until much later... They were getting the Point Of Origin, and they took out the mortar men with AH-64s.

Still in this position, and we're in the wide open, but there's streets around us leading around the city. There's these people about 300m away, peeking around the corner of this wall. My gunner and BC spot them, and I can make them out from the driver's periscope. Now, there's no reason for anyone to be on the streets in the middle of a fucking battle for the fucking city unless they were involved in the fucking fight. My BC disagreed. He told the gunner to punch up 7.62 and fire it over their heads to scare them off. I was livid. We just lost a guy, had mortars lobbed at us, and these mother fuckers probably had something to do with it. I say, "Fuck no, those are the mother fuckers walking in mortars on us, kill those fuckers!"

"Shut up! Gunner, fire coax at them."

"You better fucking kill those mother fuckers!"

"Shut the fuck up, SM! Gunner, fire."

BOOM BOOM BOOM!

....

That wasn't 7.62...

That was 25mm

Gunner, "Oops..."

I had to turn off my mic and throw off my helmet because I was dying laughing. He fucking vaporized those bastards.

To this day, I don't really know for sure if he disobeyed the BC and took those fuckers out, or if he was thinking the same as me. Maybe he thought he punched up 7.62, we had been up for over 36 hours, and it was a legit accident. Maybe he knew I was right, that those fuckers were probably involved in the battle, and were guiding in the mortars.

Oh, the SSG we lost from the IED, he was ok. We were all sure he was dead, and then 3 days later we got word back that he was still alive, and a day or two after that he was back out there with us. That dude was hardcore. He even turned down his Purple Heart Medal. I didn't even know you could do that.

I had a cousin who was a tunnel rat in Vietnam who turned down four purple heart citations and had them submitted all at the end of his tour. He had been telling his family that he was a cook at one of the big bases. (He got busted when my grandfather rotated though his alleged base and no one working in the mess knew who he was -- but the infantry guys over in the corner ALL knew him and spilled the beans.)
